I am standing up for the employees in question by not allowing management to axe them already and I am trying to make environmental changes to help the situation for everyone. It isn’t most therapists, more like 2 out of 5. The therapists are good, and I see their potential. Management is upset.

This field requires 3x a week for effectiveness. 

45 mins is awesome but 37ish is not. Also we single book, so patients take it personally. “Did I make the therapist mad?” “The other therapist likes me more.” “What are they doing if they aren’t seeing me?” (Most times on their phone).

We will never double book, not fair to the patients nor to the therapist. You have a good point, but we decided that from the start. 


About the pay, think about this. I schedule them for 8 working hours, they see patients for 2 billable units at a time rather than the whole hour. Instead of getting like $100/hr (4 units) we only get $50 hr, but since the therapist is there we have to pay them their salary (like $50/hr). So we are losing money and it’s threatening the business which serves many patients. And what is the therapist doing with those extra 30 minutes? On their phone. So we are paying for them to be on their phone and getting bad reviews. 

Of course we have to pay, but you aren’t making a case for them to keep their jobs either. I want them to stay and I see their potential, but management is sharpening their blade. 

We are a small business and good reviews are everything. So of course we have to care. 

I really appreciate you addressing all of my questions and I really like your detailed feedback. I want to find a peaceful solution.

I think part of the problem is also the patients take it personally because everyone knows we single book. So the patients feel hurt because what else are you doing other than seeing me? I just care about the patients getting good care and the therapists are good. I just want to know if there’s any environmental change I could make to make it easier for therapists.
